normalized.governing_thought: Keep buying in 2027 on a de-risked supply, pre-qualify a gated lease, and build no cell in 2027
executive_summary: Judged on four tests, not unit price, only buying with a de-risked supply fails none – Our starting hypothesis, a leased cell, failed three of the five conditions it needed

The owned cell is not a 2027 option – It needs $7.3M against the $5.0M capital limit and leaves ~$3.2M of cash, below the $4.0M floor – The circulated $27 saving is $16 per good housing in 2027; payback is 3.7 years at 100k units (7.2 at 65k)

Leasing is a cost near-tie that turns negative if any one assumption slips – It saves $0.3M (1%) over 2027–29 in the plan, but costs $1.4M more on conservative demand – It costs $0.5M more if it runs 7 months of 2027 on full fixed cost; break-even is 207k units in 2028–29

Delivery reliability is a supply-design problem that buying can fix faster than any cell – The 0.2-percentage-point shortfall (96.8% on time against 97%) traces to one flood closure – Four supply levers act in 0–13 weeks, against 5–9+ months for a cell, for $0.25M capital and ≤ $0.72M working capital

Pre-agreed gates would switch to the lease; act before the March 2027 quote expiry – Triggers: committed 2028–29 volume of 208k+, a price above ~$84 (~$74 with committed volume) or on-time delivery under 97% for two quarters – The plan keeps 2027 year-end cash near $8.2M, enough to fund the lease if a gate trips

slides.title: A five-layer supply contingency protects the 97% requirement for $0.25M of capital and up to $0.72M of working capital

claims.claim: A five-layer supply contingency protects the 97% requirement for $0.25M of capital and up to $0.72M of working capital
evidence: 1 · Buffer stock: Hold ~6 weeks (~9,600 units) to bridge the emergency notice; protects against one-week outages, road closures; immediate; up to $0.72M working capital
2 · Second source: Tool the alternate shop; split quarterly orders (~25%); single-shop failure; tooling lead time to confirm; $0.25M capital
3 · Reserved capacity: Contract the 40k reserved units; extend 2028–29 pricing by March; demand upside, capacity sold elsewhere; 90 days' notice; negotiated, no take-or-pay
4 · Emergency supplier: Framework with the second approved supplier at $88 a unit; outage that outlasts the buffer; 6 weeks' notice; ~$15 a unit: ~$0.1M a month of full outage
5 · Lease fallback: Finish site survey; hold terms; trigger only via gates (p. 14); supplier failure, sustained price rise; about 5 months; $2.0M + $1.6M a year, if triggered
Buffer = 6 weeks × 1,600 units a week (80k ÷ 50 weeks) × $75; carrying cost not yet modelled
One emergency month at 2027 volume: ~6,700 units × $15 = ~$0.1M; premium assumes $2 freight/QA on top of $88

claims.claim: Cheaper unless an outage tops a year: the lease's $1.4M conservative-case cost buys ~14 emergency months
